style.vernacular: Brick Netherlands: narrow gabled brick canal houses (red-brown and dark brick with white-framed sash windows and hoisting beams) in the old centres; interwar Amsterdam School and 1960s-80s brick and concrete housing blocks; flat polder towns (Hoofddorp, Almere, Zaandam) of brick terraces, pantile pitched roofs and glass-and-brick public buildings; glass and steel offices on the Zuidas and around Schiphol. Dark red or black glazed pantile roofs, bicycles, canals and pollarded plane or lime trees.
style.ornament: Stepped, neck, bell and spout gables on narrow canal-house fronts; hoisting beams and hooks in the gable; white-painted sash windows with shutters in dark green or black; light stone bands, lintels and cornices against dark brick; Amsterdam School brick sculpture; stone-and-water motifs in modern landscaping.

sources.what: brick as the main Dutch material (red to dark orange, darkening with age); stepped gables especially in Amsterdam; narrow canal houses with light horizontal bands; Berlage, Amsterdam School, De Stijl, Structuralism
typical late-Renaissance single-aisle Dutch reformed church (1755) in the Zaan region
anthracite-coloured brick facade and translucent PVC roof on wooden trusses as a current Dutch regional stadium
